newsitem.title: USA: US Senator against CRP for Crown Butte.
newsitem.headline: US Senator against CRP for Crown Butte.

text.p: Senate Agriculture Committee Chairman Richard Lugar said Friday that he will oppose an administration proposal to use Conservation Reserve Program funds to pay Crown Butte not to mine near Yellowstone National Park.

"I oppose this use of CRP funds ... I do not anticipate that the (Agriculture) Committee will act favorably on the Administration proposal," the Indiana Republican said in a letter to Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman dated March 14.
The administration on Wednesday offered Crown Butte $65 million to forgo mining near Yellowstone.

The money would come from mining royalties in future years, but the expense would be offset in this year's budget by delaying for one year the enrollment of two million acres into USDA's Conservation Reserve Program.
The administration recently announced a new 10-year CRP, and farmers throughout the nation are now enrolling in the program.

The administration goal is to maintain a base of 36 million acres of fragile cropland in the program, and budget assumptions were that 10-year contracts would be written this year for 19 million acres.
Under the Crown Butte plan, that amount would decrease to 17 million acres, and the two million would be enrolled the following year.
Farm groups have criticized the proposal, and said it is not fair for a successful farm program to have to help pay for an unrelated government expense.
Glickman said the plan would in no way hurt the program and that the government remains fully committed to the CRP.
Lugar said in his letter that the plan was fiscally irresponsible and ill-timed.
"It is inappropriate to fund an activity completely outside USDA's purview with funds intended by Congress to help farmers conserve our resources," Lugar said.
